title: Relative Frobenius is an integral universal homeomorphism
statement: Let $p$ be a prime and let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] of characteristic $p$ [def-weil-scheme-characteristic-p]. For any morphism of schemes $v:V\to X$, let $F_X:X\to X$ and $F_V:V\to V$ be their absolute Frobenius morphisms [def-weil-absolute-frobenius-scheme]; $V$ has characteristic $p$ because $p\cdot1$ pulls back to zero. Form the fibre product $V^{(p/X)}=V\times_{X,F_X}X$ [def-pc-fibre-product], with projections $\pi_1$ to $V$ and $\pi_2$ to $X$. Let $r_{V/X}:V\to V^{(p/X)}$ be the unique morphism with $\pi_1r_{V/X}=F_V$ and $\pi_2r_{V/X}=v$; it exists since $vF_V=F_Xv$, as follows from $v^\sharp(s^p)=v^\sharp(s)^p$. Then $r_{V/X}$ is integral [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and is a universal homeomorphism [def-weil-universal-homeomorphism]. No weakly-etale, finite-type, quasi-compactness, or perfection hypothesis is imposed on $v$, $V$, or $X$.

source.place: Tag 0CCB, lemma-relative-frobenius: the relative Frobenius is a universal homeomorphism and is integral.

proof.text: Pull back p=0 along v.appTop and restrict from global sections to every open to obtain V.IsCharacteristic p. Absolute Frobenius is natural: Scheme.Hom.ext reduces the assertion to map_pow on sections, with both base maps the identity. The pullback lift r=(F_V,v) has the two projection equations and is unique by pullback.hom_ext.

Construct the finite-field datum with a=1, q=p, k_0=ULift (ZMod p), and its AlgebraicClosure. Its cardinality is p by ZMod.card and the cardinality of ULift. For any scheme T with p=0 in global sections, ringChar.dvd gives ringChar Gamma(T,top) dividing p. Thus ZMod.castHom, composed with ULift.ringEquiv, gives a unital prime-field map to global sections, even if this is the zero ring. Compose T.toSpecGamma with Spec of this map. The existing absolute-Frobenius theorem for this datum applies to X and V, providing the IsUniversalHomeomorphism class and hence integrality, universal injectivity, and surjectivity of their Frobenii. No algebraic-closure base change of either scheme is performed.

source.place: Tag 0CC8; prime-field construction and the global-sections/spectrum adjunction.

proof.text: The projection h=pullback.fst v F_X is a base change of F_X, hence a universal homeomorphism. Since r followed by h equals F_V, both h and this composite are universal homeomorphisms. Apply the existing library theorem IsUniversalHomeomorphism.of_comp r h. Its integral component uses separatedness of h (which follows from injectivity) and IsIntegralHom.of_comp. Its other components are the field-point and surjectivity cancellations expanded in the next two steps. The absolute-Frobenius class already includes integrality, so closed-embedding affineness and integral=affine+universally-closed are unnecessary.

Apply the field-valued-point criterion for universal injectivity to r and r followed by h. For any field K and a,b:Spec K to V with a followed by r equal to b followed by r, postcompose with h and reassociate. Universal injectivity of r followed by h gives a=b.
For y in the twist, surjectivity of r followed by h supplies x with h(r(x))=h(y). Injectivity of h gives r(x)=y. This proves Surjective r, with no nonemptiness assumption.

source.place: Tag 0CCB, point-set cancellation in Morphisms lemma-permanence-universal-homeomorphism.

proof.text: Combine integrality, universal injectivity, and surjectivity into IsUniversalHomeomorphism r, then apply isUniversalHomeomorphism_le_universally_isHomeomorph to obtain the quantified topological conclusion. Pair this with the projection equations and the uniqueness established by the pullback universal property.

Tag 04DF supplies the quantified topological conclusion.

The statement matches Stacks varieties.tex 0CCB/0CC9 (l.7117/7071): fibre product V x_{X,F_X} X, r=(F_V,v), and the condition v F_V = F_X v is in the correct order. Integral and universal homeomorphism are both true for arbitrary schemes. I tested the empty scheme, v=id, F_p[e]/e^2 and an infinite polynomial ring; the last shows r is integral but not finite, as the statement says. Step 2: the specialization q=p of lem-pur-absolute-frobenius-universal-homeomorphism is valid because its closed Lean (slopmaster2 Morphisms/Frobenius.lean:149-168) works for any finite field k and any k-scheme with no finiteness hypothesis. Step 3: pi_1 is the base change of F_X along v. Step 4: 04DE plus universally closed plus 01WM make F_V integral. Step 5: h is affine, hence separated; IsIntegralHom.of_comp with f=r, g=h gives r integral. Step 6: the field-point criterion of 01S4, quoted in def-weil-radicial-morphism, gives universal injectivity. Step 7: point-set surjectivity. Step 8: lem-pc-integral-radicial-surjective-universal-homeomorphism, which is Lean-closed, gives the topological notion. proof_deps equals the union of uses. Every cited node is a definition, a Mathlib leaf or Lean-closed, and I accept the six declared tool_uses. lean.statement: theorem relativeFrobenius_integral_universalHomeomorphism (p : ℕ) (X V : Scheme.{u}) (hX : X.IsCharacteristic p) (v : V ⟶ X) : ∃ hV : V.IsCharacteristic p, ∃ r : V ⟶ pullback v (X.iterateFrobenius hX.1 (hX.2 ⊤) 1), r ≫ pullback.fst v (X.iterateFrobenius hX.1 (hX.2 ⊤) 1) = V.iterateFrobenius hV.1 (hV.2 ⊤) 1 ∧ r ≫ pullback.snd v (X.iterateFrobenius hX.1 (hX.2 ⊤) 1) = v ∧ IsIntegralHom r ∧ (topologically IsHomeomorph).universally r ∧ ∀ s : V ⟶ pullback v (X.iterateFrobenius hX.1 (hX.2 ⊤) 1), s ≫ pullback.fst v (X.iterateFrobenius hX.1 (hX.2 ⊤) 1) = V.iterateFrobenius hV.1 (hV.2 ⊤) 1 → s ≫ pullback.snd v (X.iterateFrobenius hX.1 (hX.2 ⊤) 1) = v → s = r
